project_overview.purpose: Mid-size e-commerce backend supporting product catalog, cart, checkout, and order fulfillment for a single-region online retailer
project_overview.target_users: Retail customers (web + mobile checkout), internal ops staff (order management), external logistics partners (fulfillment status updates)
project_overview.deployment_environment: Cloud, single AWS region (us-east-1), containerized services on ECS

core_features: Catalog Service (Node.js, PostgreSQL): manages product listings, pricing, and category data; maintains its own read-optimized cache of product data for fast page loads

Search Service (Python, Elasticsearch): provides full-text product search; maintains an independent local cache of product data synced from Catalog Service on a best-effort basis, with no defined consistency guarantee between the two caches
Cart Service (Node.js, Redis): manages active shopping carts per customer session
Checkout Service (Node.js): orchestrates checkout flow, validates cart contents, calculates totals and tax
Payment Service (Node.js, Stripe API): calls out to Stripe to process card payments; payment initiation is a single outbound HTTP call to Stripe's charge endpoint at checkout time

Order Service (Node.js, PostgreSQL): creates and tracks orders; maintains its own denormalized copy of product data (name, price, image URL) at order-creation time, refreshed independently of Catalog Service
Inventory Service (Java, PostgreSQL): tracks stock levels across two warehouses, decrements stock on order confirmation
Fulfillment Service (Python, ShipStation API): sends fulfillment requests to ShipStation and receives shipping status webhooks
Notification Service (Node.js, SendGrid API, Twilio API): sends order confirmation and shipping update emails/SMS
Admin Dashboard (React, internal REST API): internal web UI for ops staff to review orders, manage inventory overrides, and issue refunds
key_user_flows: Customer browses catalog via Catalog/Search Services -> adds items to Cart Service -> checks out via Checkout Service -> Payment Service charges via Stripe -> Order Service creates order -> Inventory Service decrements stock -> customer receives order confirmation
Ops staff uses Admin Dashboard to review pending orders -> allocates inventory via Inventory Service -> triggers fulfillment via Fulfillment Service
Fulfillment Service sends request to ShipStation -> ShipStation webhook updates shipping status -> Notification Service alerts customer via SendGrid/Twilio

non_functional_requirements.performance: Checkout flow must complete in under 3 seconds end-to-end under normal load; catalog page loads under 500ms
non_functional_requirements.scalability: Must support Black Friday-level traffic spikes (~10x baseline) without manual intervention
non_functional_requirements.availability: Target 99.9% uptime for checkout path; catalog browsing can tolerate brief degradation
non_functional_requirements.security: PCI compliance required for payment flow; customer PII (name, address, email, phone) stored and must be protected at rest and in transit
non_functional_requirements.observability: Centralized logging and tracing across all services; alerting on checkout failure rate and payment gateway errors

existing_systems: PostgreSQL — single instance in us-east-1a, no read replica or documented failover, backs both Catalog Service and Order Service
technical_constraints.budget_infra_limits: Single-region deployment for MVP launch; multi-region is a post-launch consideration
technical_constraints.team_skillset: Small backend team (4 engineers), comfortable with Node.js and Python, limited Java experience

data_architecture.storage_requirements: PostgreSQL for transactional data (catalog, orders, inventory) on a single instance with no replica; Redis for cart/session state; Elasticsearch for search index. Product data is independently cached or denormalized in three places (Catalog Service, Search Service, Order Service) with no single source of truth defined.
data_architecture.data_flow: Customer -> Cart Service -> Checkout Service -> Payment Service (single outbound call to Stripe charge endpoint, no documented retry or idempotency handling on failure) -> Order Service -> Inventory Service -> Fulfillment Service (ShipStation) -> Notification Service
data_architecture.retention_compliance: PCI-relevant payment data not stored directly (delegated to Stripe); customer PII retained per standard e-commerce retention policy, no formal compliance framework defined yet

open_questions: Should product data be centralized in a single source of truth service rather than duplicated across Catalog, Search, and Order services?
What is the failover plan if the single-instance PostgreSQL primary becomes unavailable?
Does Payment Service need retry/idempotency handling for the Stripe charge call, given network failures at checkout are user-facing and financially sensitive?
